original.guitar: Patrick Bourgeois or Alain Lapointe (the credits for this track were not found)
original.amp: Unknown. Typical early-90s Quebec pop-rock studio sound: clean, compressed, chorus and stereo delay
original.effects: Chorus, stereo delay, plate/hall reverb (era style, not documented)
original.notes: From the album Snob (1991). No source documents the gear on this song, so this tone follows the style of the record.

recipes.tips: Channel A for the clean, chorused verses. Switch to channel B for a light AC30 crunch in the choruses. Stomp COMP for more sustain on arpeggios. The chorus and delay are stereo: they sound widest if the mixer has the Tonelab's L and R outputs panned apart.
recipes.why: The early-90s pop-rock clean sound is a bright clean amp with chorus, a stereo delay just under the beat and a plate reverb. Both pickups, split, give a glassy, Strat-like middle-position sound.

original.amp: Unknown. Typical late-80s / early-90s Marshall-style rock crunch
original.effects: Light chorus, stereo delay, hall reverb (era style, not documented)
original.notes: From the album Snob (1991). No source documents the gear on this song, so this tone follows the style of the record.

recipes.tips: Channel A for the crunch rhythm, channel B for the lead lines. Stomp the Tube OD for extra sustain on a solo. Lower the guitar volume to 7 on channel A to clean the crunch up.
recipes.why: A JCM800-style crunch with a touch of chorus, a stereo delay and a hall reverb is the classic polished rock-lead sound of that era. The bridge humbucker gives the lead its focus.
